messages:
customer-jones: Hey — first noticed ~14:10 UTC that several users lost the 'billing-admin' role after an Okta group change. SCIM delivery shows 200 for the push but roles disappeared in our UI. tenant: t-acme-93f. Can someone look?

sasha (CS): Sorry about that, we'll investigate. Quick Q: did Okta perform a Group Rename or a Delete+Create? Also can you paste one example group externalId and a user externalId from the SCIM payload?

customer-jones: It was a rename. Display changed from 'ACME Billing' -> 'Acme-Billing'. Group externalId in the SCIM push: `okta|grp|00u1aB7C`. Example user externalId: `okta|usr|0uN7x...`. We still have the push logs if needed.

liam (ENG): grabbing provisioning traces now. Initial hypothesis: externalId normalization or member id hashing changed during the rename, which our sync interpreted as group gone -> remove members. Pushing trace link: https://redwood/logs/trace/abcd1234

liam (ENG): from audit: `operation: remove_members`, reason: `group_not_found_after_rename`, affected_users: 18.

irina (SEC): any chance the SCIM token rotated around that time? We saw a token rotation yesterday that accidentally removed the `scim:members` scope on one token which could make a members read return 403.

sasha (CS): @customer-jones can you check if the Okta SCIM connector sent a PATCH that replaced members with an empty array around 14:11 UTC? That pattern would explain the deprovision if read fallback failed.

customer-jones: Confirmed — there is a PATCH at 2026-03-15T14:11:08Z that looks like it replaced members with `[]` while the rename was in-flight. Okta support says the connector sent that during the rename operation.

liam (ENG): root cause (prelim): Okta rename produced a transient state where our mapping between externalId -> internal group id didn't match. Our sync pipeline saw the group as missing and ran a remove-members op. Concurrently a token rotate caused a `GET members` to 403 (missing `scim:members` scope), so our safety check (re-read members) failed and we committed the deprovision.

liam (ENG): repro steps: 1) Rename group in Okta (displayName change, same id) -> 2) Okta connector emits a `PATCH` with `members: []` then `PATCH` with updated displayName -> 3) Token rotation happens and the follow-up `GET /Groups/:id/members` returns 403 -> 4) pipeline treats lack of members as authoritative -> deprovision users.

sasha (CS): mitigation options: (A) run an immediate one-off member re-import from Okta export to restore roles (we can do that if you authorize), (B) re-run the last successful snapshot to restore membership, (C) short-term we can block group-originated member removals during renames. Which do you prefer?

customer-jones: Please do the one-off re-import and snapshot restore if needed. Also can we get a code fix so future renames don't deprovision users?

liam (ENG): action items: 1) I'll trigger the one-off member reimport job (ETA ~30m) and monitor; 2) implement a sync logic change: treat `PATCH members: []` + subsequent 403 read as transient and fall back to last-known member snapshot instead of deprovisioning; 3) add an alert when SCIM token scopes change or when `scim:members` calls start returning 403; 4) open RFC + PR for the fix and a migration for affected tenants.

irina (SEC): I'll coordinate token rotation policy and verify the rotated token includes `scim:members` and `scim:read`/`scim:write` scopes.

sasha (CS): I'll update the customer ticket with the plan and get explicit approval to run the reimport. :thumbsup:

liam (ENG): sample problematic SCIM payload we observed:
```
PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/00u1aB7C
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {"op":"replace","path":"members","value":[]}
  ]
}
```
liam (ENG): note: this is the transient 'empty members' push that, combined with the 403 on read, resulted in the deprovision.

sasha (CS): Thanks everyone — I'll post updates once the reimport completes and share the RFC link when ready.
